title: Understanding Pipe Slope in Drainage Systems
description: Gravity is the primary force moving waste through a residential or commercial drainage system. For gravity drainage to function reliably, horizontal pipes must maintain a consistent downward slope. If a pipe is installed too flat, wastewater slows down, allowing solid waste to settle and eventually form a blockage. Conversely, if a pipe is pitched too steeply, the liquid portion of the waste rushes past the solids, leaving heavy waste stranded behind. Proper slope ensures that both liquid and solid waste travel together at an efficient velocity, keeping the drainage lines clear and fully operational over time.

Gravity is the primary force moving waste through a residential or commercial drainage system. For gravity drainage to function reliably, horizontal pipes must maintain a consistent downward slope. If a pipe is installed too flat, wastewater slows down, allowing solid waste to settle and eventually form a blockage. Conversely, if a pipe is pitched too steeply, the liquid portion of the waste rushes past the solids, leaving heavy waste stranded behind. Proper slope ensures that both liquid and solid waste travel together at an efficient velocity, keeping the drainage lines clear and fully operational over time.
